FINDINGS_RANKED.what: PAPER 018 already carries `Evidence depth: abstract + frammenti Scholar Gateway`. Inserting a second depth line under Status leaves the false field standing and, because coverage_report and batch_queue parse `**Evidence depth:**` into a dict where the LAST occurrence wins, the stale line wins: the guard's registry side rises 63 -> 69 (it scans the whole record block) while coverage_report's full_text count rises only 66 -> 71 and PAPER 018 stays `abstract`. The act must REPLACE, not add. ATTRIBUTION: the author found the same defect independently and landed it in f81260f during my task; the two-instrument split and both measured numbers are mine.

The guard's read side is not 93. Measured: report['counts']['full text'] = 105 (62 PAPER-owned, 40 receipt-only, 3 CORPUS), and the guard compares that to the registry claim count. The prediction '93 > 69' should read '105 > 69'. The conclusion that the test stays red is right; the arithmetic supporting it is not, and 'the 30-row gap' is a 42-row gap on the instrument's own numbers.

FINDINGS_RANKED.item: CC-20260914-EVIDENCE-DEPTH-01 (the class the author routed to plan)
FINDINGS_RANKED.what: The routed class 'four PAPER records declare a depth weaker than the ledger's best receipt: 015, 018, 029, 031' is wrong in membership and in direction. Measured: 11 records declare weaker and 10 declare STRONGER, the ten being exactly the grandfathered ratchet list; 015, 029 and 031 declare a legacy full-text marker naming no receipt over a complete receipt, which is a third class (accurate rank, absent provenance). Only PAPER 018 of the four is an understatement.

The proposed Role for PMID 33058734 re-imports the framing canon withdrew the same day. DL-MECH-012 states in canon that this paper is a SPLIT result and not 'the negative': leak and histologic injury are significantly greater under LPS and MRSA, and isolated endothelial cells secrete more IL-6, KC and MCP-1 under MRSA (manifest entries[31], all three asterisked). Calling it 'the peer-reviewed null on the inflammatory-cytokine endpoints' is true only of the BALF in-vivo leg (entries[14], [16]); the paper's third cytokine measurement is positive.

The Role's causal clause is false: the 'multi-tissue convergence' argument was NOT withdrawn because of this paper. It was retired in BATCH_20260913_003 on a different ground — the legs are one laboratory's tissues and the sepsis leg is an unreviewed preprint — before this paper's split result was read. A record must not claim credit for a withdrawal it did not cause.

None of the three records as specified carries an `Evidence depth` field. Simulated: they classify abstract, abstract and filtered, the guard's registry side stays 63, and 42082822's complete reading becomes invisible to classify_depth under `filtered_out`. Item 2 would reopen exactly the gap item 1 closes unless the depth line lands in the same act.

The proposed change writes the marker into a field no instrument reads. classify_depth looks for markers in `Evidence depth` and reads Status only for filtered states, so a Status-only rewrite leaves all 17 at `catalogued`, the guard unchanged at 63 and every coverage count byte-identical. The three records it cites as its form (CORPUS P268, P261, P308) each carry a separate `**Evidence depth:**` line and classify full_text. The act as written does not close the understatement it names.

The proposed Status names the receipt but not the authorising act. Measured: 3 of 3 existing members of this class name the candidate that annotated them, so the 17 would be the only members of their class that do not. (In the depth-field class the norm is the opposite — 2 of 72 name an act — so this requirement belongs to item 3, not to item 1.)

FINDINGS_RANKED.item: CC-20260914-PLACEHOLDER-IDENTITY-01 — against my own earlier record
FINDINGS_RANKED.what: The candidate's 37/35/2 reproduces EXACTLY at ad9d1b2 and at HEAD under its published rules. My earlier 45/40/5 reproduces under none of four variants (anchored and unanchored identifier regex, whole-body PMIDs, and with or without the PAPER-twin requirement give 37/35/2, 37/35/2, 57-63/38/19-25 and 96/49/47). The author's 'the difference is the rule set, not the records' is too generous to me: under my own published method his number is the answer and mine was wrong. My 'population 94' is likewise unreproducible (85 at a67559f, 93 at ad9d1b2). The candidate's own '87' reproduces at neither HEAD — the same defect in miniature.

FINDINGS_RANKED.item: CC-20260914-PLACEHOLDER-IDENTITY-01 class B — the rule question answered
FINDINGS_RANKED.what: 'normalized to [[paper_registry_current#PAPER n]]' in the Identifier field DOES name the live record, and in CORPUS P182 and P210 the Note additionally names the authorising act ('Normalized in BATCH_20260705_001 ... placeholder retained as audit trail'). Two fields name the live record and one names the act, so these records are not silent: rule 4 is right and my F4b was wrong on both. What survives is narrower — their Status alone says only 'deep-dived — registry placeholder (lint restored)', so a Status-only query misses them, which is a defect of the query, not of the record.

All four state that their receipt is 'scratchpad, NOT appended'. Measured: all four are in the ledger, complete and chain-verified, appended by the orchestrator in d3a266d / ac6ab4d. A sentence that was true when written is now false in a record that will be read as current.

Recording the byline `Aldaz M` as printed is RIGHT, and the reason given for it is wrong. The artefact's own contrib block prints given-names 'Marcelo' with initials M at 'UT MD Anderson Cancer Center, 1808 Park Road 1C, Smithville, TX', and the sibling artefact for PMID 24330518 prints 'Aldaz C Marcelo' at the same address. The identity IS resolvable from the artefact; what the artefact does not license is normalising the printed string. The candidate conflates what to print with who it is.
